# Executive Summary
The Report Attribute Analyzer is a client-facing web application developed under the C5i BI Rationalization Suite — a product line by C5i (Course5 Intelligence) designed to help enterprises govern and rationalize their Business Intelligence assets. The tool's primary purpose is to analyze PowerBI report metadata, detect duplicate or semantically similar report attributes across multiple reports, and surface actionable governance insights to BI teams and data managers seeking to reduce redundancy and consolidate their reporting landscape.

### What the System Does
As declared in index.html, the application accepts metadata exports in Excel or CSV format (uploaded via a drag-and-drop interface defined by the .drop-zone and .drop-zone-input components in style.css). Once ingested, it performs cross-report attribute matching — comparing field names, measures, and dimensions across uploaded PowerBI report definitions. The core analytical capability is LLM-powered similarity scoring, which goes beyond exact string matching to identify semantically equivalent attributes that may be named differently across reports. Results are presented in an interactive UI and can be exported back to Excel for downstream governance workflows. These four capabilities are explicitly enumerated as hero statistics in the index.html page hero section:
Upload Excel or CSV
Cross-report attribute matching
LLM-powered similarity scoring
Export to Excel

### Core Technology Stack
The application is built as a single-page web application (SPA) using a lightweight, client-centric stack:
Bootstrap 5.3.3 is loaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net as declared in index.html, providing responsive grid and utility primitives. The custom style.css defines a comprehensive purple-themed design system using CSS custom properties (--purple, --purple-mid, --purple-light, --purple-faint) and a consistent border-radius and typography scale via var(--radius) and var(--font).

### High-Level Architecture
The architecture is intentionally frontend-first, with all UI state, rendering logic, and user interaction handled in the browser. The index.html defines the structural skeleton — including the .app-header, .page-hero, .main-content, and .app-footer layout regions — while style.css governs all visual presentation. The .main-content container is constrained to max-width: 1200px and houses .content-card components that encapsulate the upload interface, results toolbar (.results-toolbar), report cards (.report-card), attribute panels (.attributes-panel), and data tables (.data-table).
The results layer features tabbed report cards (.card-tab-btn, .report-card-body) with expandable attribute lists (.attributes-list) and similarity score columns (.score-llm, .score-match) rendered in .data-table elements. A search subsystem (.search-input-group, .search-highlight) enables real-time filtering across loaded results. The application is fully responsive, with breakpoint overrides at 768px and 480px defined at the bottom of style.css.

### Summary
In aggregate, the Report Attribute Analyzer delivers an end-to-end BI governance workflow — from metadata ingestion through intelligent duplicate detection to exportable results — packaged as a zero-dependency, browser-deployable tool under the C5i BI Rationalization Suite brand. Its use of LLM-powered scoring differentiates it from rule-based deduplication tools, making it suitable for large, organically grown PowerBI environments where attribute naming is inconsistent across teams and report authors.

# AI/ML Pipeline
The C5i BI Rationalization Suite employs a hybrid AI/ML pipeline to perform semantic attribute matching across PowerBI reports. The pipeline combines classical text similarity techniques with a large language model (LLM) to achieve high-precision cross-report attribute overlap detection. All pipeline logic resides in server.py.

### Overview
The matching pipeline operates in two stages:
Local similarity scoring — fast, deterministic methods (TF-IDF cosine similarity, Jaccard similarity, Levenshtein-based edit distance) used to pre-filter and score candidate attribute pairs.
LLM-based semantic scoring — an external LLM call used to resolve ambiguous or high-potential pairs that require deeper semantic understanding.

### Models Used
TF-IDF Vectorizer (`build_tfidf_vectorizer`)
A character-level TF-IDF model is built at runtime using scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer:
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
analyzer='char',
ngram_range=(2, 4),  # Character bi-grams to 4-grams
lowercase=True,
min_df=1
)
This model is not pre-trained or persisted — it is fit fresh on every request using all attribute names extracted from the uploaded reports. The resulting tfidf_matrix and attr_to_idx lookup dictionary are held in memory for the duration of the request.
External LLM: Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct (via Azure AI Foundry)
The primary semantic reasoning model is Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, accessed through Azure AI Foundry:
The client is instantiated per-request inside the overlap analysis route:
client = AzureOpenAI(
azure_endpoint=endpoint,
api_key=api_key,
api_version=api_version
)

### Data Pipeline and Preprocessing
Input
Users upload an Excel or CSV file containing PowerBI report metadata. The server parses this file to extract per-report attribute lists, building a dictionary of the form:
{
"ReportA": ["Revenue", "CustomerID", "Region", ...],
"ReportB": ["Total Sales", "CustID", "Territory", ...]
}
Normalization (`normalize_format`)
All attribute strings are normalized before any similarity computation:
Unicode non-breaking spaces (\u00A0) replaced with standard spaces
Zero-width spaces (\u200B) removed
Strings are stripped and lowercased
TF-IDF Matrix Construction
Once all attributes are collected across all reports, build_tfidf_vectorizer is called:
all_attributes = []
for report_attrs in reports.values():
all_attributes.extend(report_attrs)
vectorizer, tfidf_matrix, attr_to_idx = build_tfidf_vectorizer(all_attributes)
This produces a sparse matrix where each row corresponds to one attribute, enabling fast cosine similarity lookups via tfidf_similarity_score.

### Hybrid Scoring (`calculate_hybrid_match_score`)
For each candidate attribute pair (attr1, attr2), a composite score is computed combining:
TF-IDF cosine similarity — character n-gram overlap between normalized attribute names
Jaccard similarity — trigram-based set overlap (jaccard_similarity, n=3)
Edit distance similarity — normalized Levenshtein distance (1.0 - distance / max_len)
The hybrid score is used as a secondary ranking signal alongside the LLM score in the final output.

### LLM Inference Setup (`batch_llm_contextual_scores`)
LLM inference is invoked for attribute pairs that pass an initial candidate filter. The function batches pairs into groups of 25 and sends a structured prompt to the LLM:
def batch_llm_contextual_scores(
pairs: List[Tuple[str, str]],
client: AzureOpenAI,
model: str,
batch_size: int = 25
) -> Dict[Tuple[str, str], float]:
Prompt Design
The prompt instructs the model to act as a data modeling expert and score each pair on a 0.0–1.0 semantic similarity scale, returning only valid JSON:
"1.0 = Semantically Identical (e.g. 'CustID' vs 'Customer ID')"
Output ONLY valid JSON: { "1": 0.95, "2": 0.15, ... }
Low temperature (0.1) is used to minimize hallucination and enforce deterministic JSON output.
Concurrency
Batches are processed in parallel using ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=2:

future_to_batch = {executor.submit(process_batch, batch): batch for batch in batches}

summary: Single-page web app (SPA) built with Bootstrap 5.3.3; frontend-first architecture, browser-deployable with no heavy dependencies
Backend pipeline resides entirely in server.py; Python-based with scikit-learn and Azure AI Foundry integrations
Input: Excel or CSV PowerBI metadata uploads via drag-and-drop; output: exportable Excel governance reports
Data model is a per-report attribute dictionary mapping report names to lists of field/measure/dimension strings
Two-stage AI/ML pipeline: local hybrid scoring (TF-IDF, Jaccard, Levenshtein) followed by LLM semantic scoring
LLM is Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct accessed via Azure AI Foundry using AzureOpenAI client instantiated per-request
TF-IDF vectorizer is character-level (bi-gram to 4-gram), fit fresh per request — not persisted or pre-trained
LLM inference batches 25 attribute pairs per call, parallelised via ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers=2) with retry/backoff
Preprocessing normalises Unicode anomalies, strips whitespace, and lowercases all attribute strings before scoring
UI constraints: max-width 1200px content area, responsive breakpoints at 768px and 480px, purple-themed design system
NFR: deterministic LLM output enforced via low temperature (0.1) and strict JSON-only prompt instructions
Positioned as a zero-infrastructure governance tool for large PowerBI estates with inconsistent cross-team naming
